items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: I put him in the band anyhow to fill out... La Rocca used to come and sit on Saturdays and Sunday.

ctx.x: All right, he said. If you say so, it's all right. We stood by number nine, Jane Jane House, on Decatur and Espinade. I lined them all around the circle. Said to the Chinaman, I said, whenever you can catch time, the Chinaman, that you can fill up a note, put it in there. This baritone, I said, hold up as much as possible for you. All right. Put the tuba in the Chinaman's hand. Every night we played for two weeks. Every night for two weeks. Chinaman on the tube. Start to put them in parades. Start to moat around.…

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: I'm only saying this because it's so safe. It was told to me... I'm not saying that I know about this, but it was told to me.

ctx.x: The time that, the time La Rocca went up there, now I'm not sure, I'm only saying this because it's so safe. It was told to me. That some fellow would come up in a parade we were playing, from north, and wanted to know about musicians. Yes. And now, it seems to me, now I'm not saying that I know about this, but it was told to me. The Rocca then represented himself as the main squeeze.
It was one of your bands, I heard, though.
